title: Residential Lease Agreement
summary: A plain-English lease for a house, apartment or unit: rent, deposit, maintenance, entry, pets and ending the lease.
useWhen: Renting an entire home or unit to a tenant for a fixed term or month to month. For renting a room in a shared home, use the room rental agreement.
watchOuts: Security deposit limits, separate-account and interest rules, and return deadlines vary by state and sometimes by city. Check the state notes before setting the deposit.
Many cities have rent control, just-cause eviction, registration or inspection rules that override lease terms. Verify locally.

Notices of default, eviction or the right to cure for a primary residence are excluded from the federal E-SIGN Act. Serve those notices the way your state's law requires, usually on paper, even if the lease itself is signed electronically.

Fair housing: do not screen, advertise or set terms based on race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation and gender identity), national origin, familial status or disability, or other classes protected by state and local law. Many places also prohibit discrimination based on source of income.

Pre-1978 housing needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure and EPA pamphlet before the lease is signed. Many states also require disclosures about mold, flooding, bed bugs, radon or smoking policies.
Landlords cannot lock out tenants, shut off utilities or remove belongings to force a move-out. Only a court can evict.

variables.label: State where the property is located
variables.help: Two-letter code. Chucksi shows the notes for this state from the state reference (states.json): official forms, required disclosures, closing practice, notarization and recording, executory-contract and wholesaling rules.

variables.label: Landlord address for notices and rent
variables.help: Many states require the landlord to give an address for notices.

variables.label: Tenant name(s)
variables.help: Every adult who will live there should sign.

variables.label: Other occupants
variables.help: Names of minors or other people who will live there.

variables.label: Lease type
variables.help: Fixed term ends on a date. Month to month continues until notice.

variables.label: At the end of a fixed term
variables.help: What happens when the term ends.

variables.label: How rent is paid
variables.default: by electronic transfer or check to the landlord
variables.help: Methods accepted. Some states require a cash option or prohibit electronic-only payments.

variables.label: Grace period (days)
variables.help: Days before a late fee applies. Some states set a minimum.

variables.label: Late fee
variables.help: Must be reasonable. Several states cap late fees.

variables.label: Where the deposit is held
variables.help: Some states require the bank name and address, a separate account or interest.

variables.label: Pets allowed?
variables.help: Assistance animals for people with disabilities are not pets and cannot be refused just because of a no-pets rule.

variables.label: Pet terms
variables.help: Type, number, pet deposit or rent (check state limits).

variables.label: Smoking
variables.default: not allowed anywhere on the property
options: not allowed anywhere on the property
allowed only in designated outdoor areas

variables.label: Notice before landlord entry (hours)
variables.help: Many states require 24 or 48 hours, except emergencies.

variables.label: Require renters insurance?
variables.help: Protects the tenant's belongings and liability.

variables.label: Notice to end a month-to-month tenancy (days)
variables.help: Check the state's minimum. Some cities require more or require just cause.

variables.label: Built before 1978?
variables.help: Adds the lead warning statement. Also sign the full federal disclosure form.

sections.title: 1. Parties and property
sections.body:
**Landlord:** {{landlord_name}}, {{landlord_address}} ({{landlord_email}})

**Tenant:** {{tenant_name}} ({{tenant_email}})

Landlord rents to Tenant the residence at {{property_address}} (the "Premises"), in {{state}}, for use only as a private residence by Tenant and these occupants: {{occupants}}.

sections.title: 2. Furnishings
sections.body: The Premises are furnished. The furniture and appliances are listed in an attached inventory that both parties sign at move-in.

sections.title: 3. Term
sections.body: The lease starts on {{start_date}} and is a {{term_type}} tenancy.

sections.title: 4. Fixed term
sections.body: The lease ends on {{end_date}}. At the end of the term, the lease {{after_term}}.

sections.title: 5. Month to month
sections.body: Either party may end the tenancy by giving written notice at least {{notice_days}} days before the end of a rental period, or longer if the law requires.

sections.title: 6. Rent
sections.body: Rent is {{rent}} per month, due on day {{due_day}} of each month, paid {{payment_method}}. First month's prorated rent, if any: {{prorated_first}}. If rent is not received within {{grace_days}} days after the due date, Tenant will pay a late fee of {{late_fee}}, to the extent allowed by law. A returned payment may result in a fee allowed by law. Landlord will give receipts on request.

sections.title: 7. Security deposit
sections.body: Tenant pays a security deposit of {{deposit}} before move-in. It is not a limit on Tenant's liability and may not be used by Tenant as the last month's rent unless Landlord agrees in writing. Deposit held at: {{deposit_held}}. After Tenant moves out and returns the keys, Landlord will return the deposit, with any interest the law requires, minus lawful deductions for unpaid rent and damage beyond normal wear and tear. Landlord will include an itemized statement of deductions within the deadline set by the law of {{state}}, sent to the forwarding address Tenant provides.

sections.title: 8. Move-in and move-out condition
sections.body: Before or at move-in, the parties will complete a written move-in checklist, with photos, signed by both. Tenant will leave the Premises clean and in the same condition at move-out, except for normal wear and tear.

sections.title: 9. Utilities
sections.body: Tenant pays: {{utilities_tenant}}. Landlord pays: {{utilities_landlord}}. Tenant will set up accounts in Tenant's name for utilities Tenant pays, starting on the start date.

sections.title: 10. Maintenance and repairs
sections.body: Landlord will keep the Premises in a safe and habitable condition, comply with building and health codes, and make necessary repairs within a reasonable time after notice, as the law requires. Tenant will keep the Premises clean and sanitary, use appliances and fixtures properly, replace smoke-alarm batteries if applicable, promptly report needed repairs, water leaks and mold in writing, and pay for damage caused by Tenant, occupants or guests beyond normal wear and tear. Tenant will not make alterations, paint or change locks without Landlord's written consent.

sections.title: 11. Landlord entry
sections.body: Landlord may enter at reasonable times to inspect, make repairs, or show the Premises, after giving at least {{entry_notice_hours}} hours' notice (or longer if the law requires), and at any time in an emergency.

sections.title: 12. Use and conduct
sections.body: Tenant will follow the law and any written community rules, not disturb neighbors, and not allow illegal activity on the Premises. Smoking (including vaping and cannabis) is {{smoking}}. Parking: {{parking}}. Guests staying more than 14 days in any six-month period need Landlord's written consent, to the extent the law allows.

sections.title: 13. Pets
sections.body: Pets are allowed on these terms: {{pet_terms}}. Tenant is responsible for any damage or nuisance caused by pets. Assistance animals for people with disabilities are handled under fair housing law, not this section.

sections.title: 14. No pets
sections.body: Unless the Pets section is included, no pets are allowed without Landlord's written consent. This does not apply to assistance animals for people with disabilities, which are handled under fair housing law.

sections.title: 15. Renters insurance
sections.body: Tenant will keep renters insurance with at least {{insurance_amount}} of personal liability coverage and provide proof on request. Landlord's insurance does not cover Tenant's belongings.

sections.title: 16. Assignment and subletting
sections.body: Tenant may not assign this lease or sublet any part of the Premises, including short-term rentals, without Landlord's written consent, which Landlord will not unreasonably withhold where the law requires.

sections.title: 17. Default and ending the lease
sections.body: If Tenant fails to pay rent or materially breaches this lease, Landlord may end the tenancy only by giving the notice and following the court process required by the law of {{state}}. Landlord will not lock out Tenant, shut off utilities or remove Tenant's belongings without a court order. If Tenant moves out early, Tenant remains responsible for rent until the earlier of the end of the term or the date a new tenant begins paying, and Landlord will make reasonable efforts to re-rent, as the law requires. Some states give tenants the right to end a lease early, for example for active military duty (federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act) or for domestic violence.

sections.title: 18. Lead-based paint warning
sections.body:
**Lead Warning Statement.** Housing built before 1978 may contain lead-based paint. Lead from paint, paint chips, and dust can pose health hazards if not managed properly. Lead exposure is especially harmful to young children and pregnant women. Before renting pre-1978 housing, lessors must disclose the presence of known lead-based paint and/or lead-based paint hazards in the dwelling. Lessees must also receive a federally approved pamphlet on lead poisoning prevention.

Landlord and Tenant will also sign the full federal Lead-Based Paint Disclosure, and Tenant acknowledges receiving the EPA pamphlet "Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home." Tenant: [[initial:tenant]]

sections.title: 19. Required disclosures
sections.body: Landlord will provide all disclosures required by federal, state and local law (see the state notes for {{state}}), for example the identity of the owner or manager, mold, flood, radon or bed bug information, as applicable. Tenant acknowledges receiving any attached disclosures. Tenant: [[initial:tenant]]

sections.title: 20. State-specific requirements
sections.body: The property is in {{state}}. The parties will comply with that state's requirements for this transaction, including required seller disclosures and forms, licensing rules, closing and recording requirements, and any mandatory statutory notices. Chucksi shows a summary of known requirements for {{state}} with this template. That summary is a starting point, may be incomplete or out of date, and is not part of this agreement. Any addendum or disclosure form the state requires will be attached and signed by the parties.

sections.title: 21. Notices
sections.body: Routine communications may be sent by email. Legal notices, including notices to pay rent, cure a breach, terminate or vacate, will be delivered as required by the law of {{state}}, which may require paper delivery or posting, and also by email when allowed. Tenant's notice address is the Premises unless Tenant gives another in writing.

sections.title: 22. Additional terms
sections.body: {{additional_terms}}

sections.title: 23. General
sections.body: This lease is governed by the law of {{state}}, and local ordinances where the Premises are located. Any term that conflicts with mandatory tenant protections is unenforceable to that extent, and the rest of the lease stays in effect. Each tenant who signs is jointly and severally responsible for all obligations. This is the entire agreement and can be changed only in writing signed by both parties. It may be signed electronically and in counterparts.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Landlord** — {{landlord_name}}

[[sig:landlord]]

Printed name: [[name:landlord]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:landlord:Title]]
Date: [[date:landlord]]

**Tenant** — {{tenant_name}}

[[sig:tenant]]

Printed name: [[name:tenant]]
Date: [[date:tenant]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Chucksi open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Real estate contracts carry state-specific disclosure, licensing, closing and recording rules. If a real estate licensee is involved, the licensee may be required to use state-promulgated or approved forms instead of this one (for example in Texas and Colorado). Deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust usually must be notarized and recorded; an electronic signature on this document does not record anything.
